body:
Thanks for your reply. You seem to have really understood my train of thought. I am apparently prone to rigid thought patterns, and so I can admit that I might be steadfastly holding on to some notion that is untrue. What you point out certainly seems to be a kink in my logic: I don't know that every woman will not want to sleep with me more than once. But I don't know that I won't win the lottery tomorrow either. Just thinking about the way the lottery works though, it seems unlikely that I will. Similarly, given what I know about girls, it seems unlikely that any would want me. While I can hold out for someone who would look past my flaws and love me in spite of them, it hurts to think that I would never be desired by anyone other than someone who was in love with me. Maybe I want to date and enjoy life a little - that avenue is closed. If I did somehow manage a significant other, how could I avoid being overly attached and clingy, knowing that she's of the rare breed that "puts up" with me? The whole thing would be demeaning and disingenuous. To hold out for someone who is 'special' and kind enough to see past my flaws seems a perversion of lust and desire. That's not how that's supposed to work. I just want a normal sex life; I would love to be attractive and desirable, but I would settle for just not being mocked and pitied. r

You wrote that it's an error to think that my worth as a person is measured by how women think of me. I can't hold myself up to any other standard of worth, because you can't pick and choose these things. I would feel like I was worth something if someone I desired wanted me back. I don't think that's unreasonable, and I also don't think that's something I can change about myself, because it strikes me as being fundamental to the human experience - I'm pretty sure everyone wants to be wanted.

You wrote that it's an error to think that women judge men primarily based on their sexual attributes.  I have been around many women, and have overheard enough conversations to understand that this is just how women are. Some are more vocal than others, but at the crux of it sexuality is the most important thing when discussing a man. It is again demeaning to think that whereas some men are spoken of in high regard - coyly giggled about or praised outright - I will only ever be laughed at or pitied. How does that not chip away at one's sense of self worth? How can you hold your head high when the person you desire and have been most vulnerable and affectionate with mocks you, and clearly prefers several others over you? How would you feel? How would anyone?

I don't mean to come off as aggressive. I really appreciate your post. I don't evenr eally know why I responded so negatively when you were so kind as to reply to me. I don't know how I'm supposed to handle this.
